newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/yen vulnerable on 115.55 prop break.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/yen vulnerable on 115.55 prop break.

text.p: Dollar/yen is perched precariously around a two-week rising trendline near 115.55 and while the dollar has yet to completely lose its grip, it is showing little inclination to move higher, analyst said.

"If we lose this 115.55 (yen) we're going to go lower and test 115.10, a loss there gives us 114.50 or so. So dollar/yen looks weak and the upside looks limited," said Scott Siller, a senior technical analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch.
Siller placed minor support at 115.30 yen and said a move to his target in the 114.50 to 114 area would be corrective to the recovery from the 111.98 low on May 20.
Some analysts look for a steeper decline, with a high probability of the cycle low being taken out.

"My bias is dollar/yen is going to continue going down and get back below 114.50," said Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America in New York, adding he sees the dollar falling below 112 yen.
Technical studies were throwing off sell signals on Thursday said Randolph Donney, director of capital markets research at Pegasus Econometric Group.
"(I'm) looking for confirmation on a break down below 115 yen. The potential there is for a move down to the low 113 area over the next couple of days," Donney said.
In contrast, dollar/mark is still in an uptrend and should zero in on its May 28 high at 1.7389, analysts said.
"Dollar/mark is a little bit the opposite (from dollar/yen). It looks like it's in an ascending triangle pattern and could push to 1.7350/1.7390," Siller said.
You may see a couple days of churning but I think eventually we're going to break out of the old high at 1.7390 (marks)," Donney said.
An outside target would be 1.7460, analysts said.
The 1.7450/70 mark level represents a high from June 1993, which the dollar touched twice before sliding to lows around 1.5870 marks in September of that year, analysts said.
At 1320 EDT/1720 GMT on Thursday, the dollar was trading at 1.7280/90 marks, off a touch from 1.7285/95 at the open and at 115.50/60 off from 115.62/72.
